scores.evidence: The title asks one clear question: how an iPad sketch reaches the local coding agent. The subtitle names the audience (new engineers) and the scope.

Five of the six boxes are runtime units. '.vibeprint dir' is a storage directory and 'Agent + MCP' combines an external agent with the vibeprint MCP server, so the box levels are slightly mixed. There is no linked zoom-in view.

The main path is covered, and the omissions are stated in the 'Outside this view' line. The relay's identity and token handshake appear only in a note, and the daemon's serving of the web app is not drawn.

The labels are short ('HTTPS req', 'tunnel WS', 'LAN strokes'), and the Claude edge is reduced to the footnote 'F1'. Solid, dashed and dotted lines are hard to tell apart at this size. The 'sketch, graph' arrow looks double-headed, and the 'tool calls' line winds around the right side of the Developer machine frame before reaching the daemon. Nothing shows ordering, or that the relay path and the LAN path are alternatives.

Four labelled frames separate device, hosted relay, developer machine and Anthropic, and their captions say which parts are optional, managed or self-hosted. The 'LAN strokes' line passes through the Hosted relay frame, which suggests the LAN path goes via the relay. The 'Developer machine ]' label breaks onto a second line.

There is a clear left-to-right direction. However, the diagram fills only about 60% of the 1194x834 canvas, and the box text and notes are roughly 8px, which is hard to read on an iPad. The 'tool calls' and 'marks (lock)' labels are crowded and collide near the agent box, and the LAN line runs underneath the relay.

There is a key for frames, boxes and line styles. Everything is drawn in the same red, and kind is shown only as a text prefix with no shape difference. The dash styles barely show at this size, so the line-style key does little work.

Three notes cover the relevant local failure points: relay backoff with LAN fallback, the token required on tunneled requests, and the files.lock fallback with a 503. Each cites a source file, and all three match the code. The Claude API being optional is mentioned in a box. None of these are attached to the edges they describe.

The footer gives the date, the revision (dca6c85 plus local edits), 'Owner: Unassigned' and 'Live runtime NOT verified'. The notes match src/server/relay.ts:206-207 and src/mcp/backend.ts:106,148. With no production check and no owner, it cannot score higher than 3.

The boxes and notes give a reasonable picture. Small text, the edge meaning hidden behind 'F1', ambiguous routing and indistinct line styles mean a newcomer could misread whether the LAN path goes through the relay.

coldRead: The iPad runs the Sketch app (React and Vite). It reaches the Daemon on the developer machine in one of two ways: directly over the LAN, or through an optional hosted Relay. In the relay case, the daemon itself opens a WebSocket tunnel out to the relay, and the iPad's HTTPS requests are forwarded over it. The daemon interprets the strokes and keeps the sketch and graph in the .vibeprint directory. If an API key is set, it also sends the sketch image to the Claude API for a handwriting pass. A coding agent uses vibeprint's MCP tools, which call the daemon. If the daemon is not running, the MCP tools write marks straight into .vibeprint/ under a lock file and return a 503 after 5 seconds of contention. If the relay goes down, the daemon retries with backoff and the LAN URL keeps working. Requests that come through the relay still need the access token.
inaccuracies: The 'LAN strokes' edge is drawn through the Hosted relay frame. In the code the LAN path goes straight to the daemon (src/server/daemon.ts) and never touches relay/.
The 'sketch, graph' edge between the Daemon and .vibeprint dir appears double-headed, while the key and the map define it as a one-way local write.
The Daemon to Claude API edge is reduced to the code 'F1', so the edge's meaning is only in a footnote rather than on the line.
The 'Agent + MCP' box combines the external coding agent with vibeprint's own MCP server (src/mcp/), so the code's ownership is unclear.
improvements: Scale the diagram to fill the 1194x834 viewport with text at least 12px, and put 'sketch image (sync)' directly on the Claude edge instead of the F1 footnote.

Route 'LAN strokes' under or around the Hosted relay frame instead of through it, mark the relay and LAN paths as alternatives, and route 'tool calls' straight to the daemon so it doesn't cross other lines.

Add non-color signals for sync, async and local edges and for node kind: thicker or clearly different dashes, plus a distinct shape for storage (e.g. a cylinder) and for external services. Split the agent from the vibeprint MCP server. Attach each failure note to its edge with a numbered marker.
